# Genesis Apocryphon Column 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Genesis Apocryphon Column 19 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 19:1 — "looking at it" / "surveying it"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "looking-at-it" | Literal rendering of Aramaic |
| LOGOS | "looking at it" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "surveying it as I went" | Dynamic; implies purposeful inspection |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "looking at it." PNEUMA's "surveying" imports a technical connotation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:2 — "Great Sea" / "Mediterranean"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Great-Sea" | Literal Aramaic designation |
| LOGOS | "the Great Sea" | Formal; preserves ancient name |
| PNEUMA | "the Mediterranean" | Dynamic; modern geographical name |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the Great Sea." The ancient designation is the scroll's own term and should be preserved.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:3 — "mountain of the Bull" / "Taurus"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-mountain of-the-Bull" | Literal translation of tur tora |
| LOGOS | "the mountain of Taurus" | Formal; identifies the geographical name |
| PNEUMA | "the Taurus Mountains" | Dynamic; modern geographical form |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "the mountain of Taurus" as a compromise: it identifies the place name while preserving the singular form of the Aramaic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:7-9 — "seed" / "descendants"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your-seed" | Literal rendering of Aramaic zar'akha |
| LOGOS | "your seed" | Formal; preserves biblical term |
| PNEUMA | "your descendants" | Dynamic; modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "descendants" as a compromise. While "seed" is the literal term, "descendants" is clearer for a consensus text and avoids the agricultural metaphor in extended passages.

**Status:** Resolved as compromise (PNEUMA's term in LOGOS's structure).

---

## 19:10 — "Rise up" / "Arise" / "Get up"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Rise-up" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "Arise" | Formal; traditional biblical diction |
| PNEUMA | "Get up" | Dynamic; colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "Arise." This is the established biblical English for divine commands and matches the register of divine speech.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:14 — "friends" / "allies"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my-friends" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "my friends" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "my allies" | Dynamic; emphasizes covenant relationship |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's "allies." In the context of the ancient Near East, Mamre, Ornam, and Eshkol are treaty partners (cf. Gen 14:13), not merely personal friends.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA.

---

## 19:19 — "sought to cut down" / "meaning to chop down"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sought to-cut-down" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "sought to cut down" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "meaning to chop down" | Dynamic; "chop" more vivid |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "sought to cut down." "Chop" is too informal for a prophetic dream sequence.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 19:25 — Pronoun direction (who is threatened)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "They-will-seek to-kill me and-to-spare you" | Sarai is the cedar (threatened) |
| LOGOS | "They will seek to kill you and to spare me" | Abram is the cedar (threatened) |
| PNEUMA | "They will try to kill you but spare me" | Abram is the cedar (threatened) |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/PNEUMA reading. The cedar represents Abram (the one threatened), and the palm represents Sarai (who cries out to save him). Sarai understands the dream: men will want to kill Abram to take her, so she proposes the sister ruse. EMET's reversal of pronouns contradicts the narrative logic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 19:25 — "mercy" / "kindness"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-mercy" | Literal rendering of Aramaic |
| LOGOS | "the mercy" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "the one kindness" | Dynamic; specifies singularity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Compromise: "the kindness." The Aramaic term is closer to hesed/kindness than to mercy, and PNEUMA's emphasis on "one" captures the urgency, though "alone" is used instead.

**Status:** Resolved as compromise.

---

## 19:29 — "in my grief" / "in my anguish"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "in-my-grief" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "in my grief" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "in my anguish" | Dynamic; stronger emotion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS rendering "in my grief." "Anguish" is stronger than the Aramaic warrants at this point.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

*Total disagreements: 9*
*Resolution: LOGOS 6, PNEUMA 1, Compromise 2, EMET 0*
